title: India Have Just Won by an Innings and 300 Runs. The ODI Series Will Be Harder.
excerpt: With Kohli injured, Bumrah rested, and Rashid Khan returning for Afghanistan, the three-match ODI series starting in Dharamshala on June 13 will be India's first real white-ball test of the summer.
body:
India have just finished dismantling Afghanistan by an innings and 300 runs in New Chandigarh — the largest innings victory in their Test history. On Saturday, the same two teams will begin a very different kind of contest. Three One-Day Internationals, starting at the HPCA Stadium in Dharamshala on June 13, moving to Lucknow's Ekana Stadium on June 17, and ending at the MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai on June 20.

The Test was a mismatch. The ODIs will not be.

## India's Squad: Big Names, Big Questions

Shubman Gill captains the side again, with Shreyas Iyer as his vice-captain. But the squad tells a complicated story. Virat Kohli is out with the hamstring injury he picked up during the IPL final. Jasprit Bumrah has been rested entirely. Rohit Sharma and Hardik Pandya are both included but their participation depends on fitness clearances that have not yet been confirmed.

If Rohit passes his fitness test, India will field a formidable top order: Rohit, Jaiswal, Gill, Iyer, and KL Rahul. If he does not, the batting order becomes a puzzle that Gill will have to solve on the fly.

The most intriguing selections are further down the list. Ishan Kishan returns to the ODI setup for the first time since the 2023 World Cup, having rebuilt his career through domestic cricket after a long exile. Prince Yadav, the Lucknow Super Giants pacer, is in line for his international debut. Washington Sundar and Nitish Kumar Reddy, both fresh off impressive performances in the Test, carry their form into the white-ball leg.

Kuldeep Yadav will be India's primary spinner, and with Prasidh Krishna and Arshdeep Singh leading the pace attack in Bumrah's absence, the bowling unit has a blend of experience and youth.

## Afghanistan's ODI Squad: Rashid Khan Returns

This is where the conversation changes. Afghanistan's Test squad was without Rashid Khan, and it showed. Their ODI squad is a different animal altogether. Rashid, one of the greatest limited-overs bowlers of his generation, returns alongside Azmatullah Omarzai and Mohammad Nabi — the veteran all-rounder who brings calm to every middle order he walks into.

Ibrahim Zadran arrives in Dharamshala riding a career-best. He scored an unbeaten 120 against Zimbabwe last week, sealing a series with an eight-wicket win. Rahmanullah Gurbaz, who did not fire in the Test, is an explosive opener who can take any bowling attack apart in the powerplay. And Rahmat Shah, fresh from his milestone of 1,000 Test runs, has been batting with the kind of assurance that suggests he is at the peak of his powers.

Afghanistan have beaten India in ODIs before. They nearly did it at the 2023 World Cup. With Rashid Khan bowling through the middle overs on pitches that could offer turn, this series is far from a foregone conclusion.

## The Bigger Picture: Road to 2027

These three ODIs are not just about the result on the scoreboard. India are building toward the 2027 ODI World Cup in Africa, and every selection, every combination, every middle-over strategy is being evaluated through that lens. Chief selector Ajit Agarkar has been clear that this home season is an audition.

Who bats at No. 4 if Kohli is unavailable long-term? Can Prince Yadav be the backup seamer for Bumrah in ICC events? Is Ishan Kishan a genuine option at No. 5, or is he a nostalgia pick? These are the questions that Dharamshala, Lucknow, and Chennai will begin to answer.

## How to Watch

In India, the series will be broadcast on Star Sports and streamed live on JioHotstar. In the United States and Canada, Willow TV carries the matches. All three ODIs are day-night fixtures, starting at 1:30 PM IST.

For NRI fans on the West Coast, that translates to 1:00 AM Pacific — the kind of pre-dawn start time that separates the devoted from the casual. For East Coast viewers, 4:00 AM is only slightly more civilized. But with Rashid Khan bowling to Rohit Sharma in the Himalayan twilight, the alarm will be worth setting.

The series also marks the end of India's home engagements before they head to Ireland for two T20Is on June 26 and 28, and then to England for five T20Is and three ODIs starting July 1. The road gets harder from here. Dharamshala is where it begins.
